body.purpose: Default UI text; capture input at 14.5px.

number.purpose: Ages, counts, dates, ticket heads. Tabular mono.

shadows.name: ticket

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Picked-up or floating paper: hover, detail panel, auth ticket, menus, toasts, sheets.

shadows.name: focus-halo

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single easing for all transitions and keyframes.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Colour, border, focus halo, keycap fade.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Row lift, capture preview strip, menu pop, toast leave.

motion.name: state-slow
motion.purpose: Toast and sheet pop, rail ticket swing, capture slot width, strength bars.

motion.name: print
motion.purpose: New ticket prints in: clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0), translateY(-6px) to none.

motion.name: tear
motion.purpose: Signature: done tears the ticket off. 35%: translateY(-3px) rotate(-0.8deg); 100%: translateY(-22px) rotate(-3deg), opacity 0, blur(1px).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all animation and transition durations.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Sidebar collapses to a 64px icon rail; detail panel floats; search collapses.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Kitchen Pass"**

Demands arrive like orders at a kitchen pass. Each one prints as a numbered ticket on thermal paper with its age running, hangs on a steel rail while it is being worked, and gets torn off when done. The application shell is the kitchen's brushed steel: a cool grey ground and a darker sidebar that never carry content of their own. Everything that *is* a demand, or is written onto one, is paper: off-white, near-black receipt ink, a 3px corner, a faint ticket shadow.

The density is that of an expediter's station: 48px rows, 6px between them, every row readable at a glance from the sequence number, title, due tag and elapsed age. Colour is rationed by heat. Fire red means urgent or overdue, heat-lamp amber means due today or aging, and everything else stays ink on paper or ink on steel. Numbers that measure something (ticket numbers, ages, counts, dates, keycaps) are set in JetBrains Mono; everything a person reads as language is Archivo.

The dark theme is the same kitchen after hours: blackened steel shell, tickets as dim warm paper (#2c2b29), inks lifted, fire and heat brightened so they still read as alarms.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials, steel and paper, each with its own ink set.
Numbered tickets with perforated (scalloped) edges where paper is torn from the printer.
A steel rail that holds in-progress tickets; done tears the ticket off.
Heat-coded colour: fire for burning, heat for warming, nothing else shouts.
Keyboard-first: keycaps are first-class, visible elements.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Paper carries receipt ink (ink, ink-2, ink-3); steel carries steel ink (steel-ink, steel-ink-2). A control that changes material changes ink with it: the search field is steel at rest and becomes paper with receipt ink on focus.

rules.name: The Heat Rule
rules.body: Fire marks what is burning (urgent, overdue), heat marks what is warming (due today, high priority, aging). Neither is ever a decorative accent, a brand colour, or a large surface; they appear as small marks, text, and soft tag fills.

rules.name: The Status Fill Rule
rules.body: Wait blue and done green appear only as tag fills, segmented selections and tick states. They never colour a ticket, a row, or a section.

rules.name: The Measurement Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Ticket numbers, elapsed ages, counts, dates, times and keycaps are JetBrains Mono with tabular figures. Words, including status and priority names, are never mono.

rules.name: The Honest Age Rule
rules.body: Every open ticket shows its elapsed age (5h, 1d, 40min) right-aligned in mono; it warms to heat and then fire as it ages.

rules.name: The Paper Weight Rule
rules.body: Only paper casts shadows, and only the two paper shadows exist. Hover lifts paper from Ticket to Lift; it never changes the paper colour.

dos: **Do** put every demand, field and floating surface on paper (paper fill, paper-edge stroke, 3px or 6px corner, ticket shadow) and leave the shell as flat steel.
**Do** switch ink with material: receipt ink on paper, steel ink on steel, including focus outlines.
**Do** set ticket numbers, ages, counts, dates and keycaps in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures, and prefix ticket numbers "Nº" on tickets, toasts and the detail head.
**Do** separate sections inside a ticket with a 1px dashed paper-edge tear line, and perforate the edge a ticket was torn from.
**Do** mark completion with the tear (260ms) and creation with the print (280ms), both on the shared ease-out curve.
**Do** colour urgency by heat: fire for urgent and overdue, heat for due today, high priority and aging.
**Do** show the keyboard shortcut as a keycap wherever an action has one.
donts: **Don't** use fire or heat as a brand accent, button fill or large surface; they are alarms.
**Don't** colour a ticket or row background by status; status lives in tags, marks, ages and group titles.
**Don't** add shadows to steel or invent a third paper shadow; paper is Ticket at rest and Lift when picked up.
**Don't** set words (status names, labels, headings) in mono, or numbers that measure in Archivo.
**Don't** round a ticket (row, rail ticket, detail panel, auth ticket) beyond 3px; the near-square corner is part of the material. Fields, menus, sheets and toasts take 6px.
